en: Jose Rizal studied ophthalmology in Europe to cure his mother's cataracts, demonstrating how medical science directly helps families.
The Philippine Carabao provides nutrient-rich milk that contains more fat and protein than cow's milk, supporting children's physical growth.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm and safe in rural clinics without electricity.
The Ifugao muyong woodlot system prevents soil erosion and filters rainwater, ensuring a clean and safe water supply for rice terraces.
The Department of Health runs the National Immunization Program to protect all Filipino children from dangerous, preventable diseases like measles.
During the Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate homes with kiping made from ground rice and natural plant dyes, ensuring non-toxic decorations.
The coconut tree provides virgin coconut oil, which contains lauric acid that has natural antibacterial properties to protect skin health.
The law recognizes Filipino Sign Language as the national sign language, helping deaf citizens safely understand emergency broadcasts and public information.
The cultural value of bayanihan improves community disaster safety because neighbors physically help each other evacuate during strong typhoons.
In 1898, the revolutionary government established the first national Board of Health to protect Filipinos from infectious diseases like cholera.
The Sampaguita, our national flower, contains essential oils that traditional folk medicine uses to safely relieve headaches and reduce fever.
The Philippine Constitution guarantees the right to health, requiring the government to provide free medical treatment in public hospitals for poor patients.
